intended_object: For a morphism of short complexes f : S₁ ⟶ S₂ and an object X, the induced map coker(Hom(X, S₁.X₂) → Hom(X, S₁.X₃)) → coker(Hom(X, S₂.X₂) → Hom(X, S₂.X₃)), with Hom written as degree-0 Ext. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in the naturality lemmas for covariantCokernelIso.
explanation: The body is `cokernel.map` applied to the commutative square formed by composing with f.τ₂ and f.τ₃ (as degree-0 Ext classes) and the two maps 'compose with Sᵢ.g'. Commutativity is proved from associativity of Ext composition in degree 0, `mk₀_comp_mk₀` and `f.comm₂₃`, so this is exactly the canonical map between the cokernels. It is stated for any abelian category with HasExt, any morphism of short complexes and any object X, which is the natural generality. It is largely a helper for the naturality of covariantCokernelIso, the identification of this cokernel with Ext¹(X, S.X₁) when S is short exact and Ext¹(X, S.X₂) vanishes. Since it still has a clear mathematical meaning (the induced map on cokernels), I judged it faithful; 'not_a_mathematical_object' would also be defensible. I found no dedicated Mathlib declaration for it; it is a direct instance of the general `cokernel.map`.
